items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: there were a few pianists that I thought I could copy, like Horace Silver and Bobby Timmons

ctx.x: Were you playing — the piano you were playing at the time, was it classical music or were you learning chords and trying to copy jazz pianists?

I was. I was, you know I was taking classical lessons, like I say my mother started me at the Wurtlitzer School of Music in downtown Buffalo when I was about eight. And they had a deal going that if you bought a new piano you got a year or two of free lessons with the piano. So me and my big sister, we both availed ourself, and we’d go for lessons. And then after that ran out then my mother hired a piano teacher who came by the house you know. And so we were doing all the regular you know piano primer books, but…

I just was reading a book about early rock & roll and the chitlin’ circuit and how popular guys like Roy Brown were at the time in the mid-50s. I’m wondering if that music, which was — we used to think of it was pre-rock & roll, or R&B, was that something you listened to? And also I wonder what did your parents like having played in the house? What kind of music?
